title: Runtime experiment feedback loop protocol
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview:
This page defines the experiment feedback loop protocol used by the Serving Runtime team to design, run, and act on profiling and kernel scheduling experiments that change runtime behavior. The protocol standardizes hypothesis framing, telemetry instrumentation, safety gates, analysis artifacts, and rollout rules. It is intended for engineers running microbenchmarks, shadow traffic experiments, and online canaries that touch the kernel scheduler, KV cache, batching heuristics, and model variant routing.

Why we have a formal protocol:
- Reduce noisy experiments and ensure reproducible results.
- Protect SLOs and customer traffic during investigations.
- Provide clear handoffs from experimenters to runtime operators and release engineers.

Scope:
Applies to experiments that: 1) modify kernel scheduler configuration or code paths, 2) alter request shaping / admission, 3) introduce new telemetry or sampling, or 4) change runtime fallback/degradation modes. Not intended for purely offline model evaluation.

Roles and ownership:
- Experiment Owner: engineer who proposes and executes the experiment (primary contact).
- Runtime Oncall: SRE responsible for live traffic safety gates (will have emergency rollback authority).
- Observability Owner: platform engineer who validates instrumentation and dashboards.
- Release Captain: release engineer who approves any rollout to Dedicated or Hosted clusters.

High-level workflow (5 phases):
1) Hypothesis & Safety Plan
   - Write a short hypothesis: "Changing kernel X threshold will reduce p99 latency by >=10% for short sequences without increasing p99 for long sequences."
   - Identify safety SLOs (see table below) and define abort thresholds.
   - Pre-validate on playground or shadow cluster.
2) Instrumentation & Baseline
   - Add required metrics and trace points.
   - Run baseline collection for at least 3 steady-state runs (48h recommended for production-like signals).
3) Controlled rollout (shadow -> canary -> ramp)
   - Start with offline shadowing, then small canary (1% traffic) with strict abort gates, then staged ramps.
4) Analysis and Signal Extraction
   - Produce an Experiment Report (templated). Include causal attribution, raw traces, and kernel-level timeline.
5) Action: revert, iterate, or promote
   - If passing gates, schedule full rollout and add config to runtime feature flags.

Safety SLOs and abort thresholds (default values):
| Signal | Baseline window metric | Abort threshold (quick abort) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| p50 latency (inferred) | baseline median | +25% | Detects immediate regressions for short ops |
| p95 latency | baseline p95 | +15% | Sensitive to medium tail widening |
| p99 latency | baseline p99 | +10% | Critical — immediate abort if exceeded repeatedly |
| error rate (5xx/transport) | baseline error rate | +100% relative or absolute >0.5% | Transport / kernel faults |
| kernel watchdog restarts | 0 in baseline window | any occurrence | Immediate abort and system investigation |

Instrumentation checklist:
- Metrics: per-route p50/p95/p99, token-throughput, queue-depth per scheduler slot, kernel-run-time distributions (ms), kvcache-hit-rate, model-variant-fallback-count.
- Tracing: attach request-id, kernel-id, scheduling-decision-id, tenant-id, model-version.
- Logs: structured JSON with kernel signals (fields: timestamp, kernel_phase, gpu_id, free_mem_mb, queue_len).
- Sampling policy: pid-based stratified sampling + entropy-aware tail amplification.

Experiment Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Fill Experiment Form (template attached) with hypothesis, owner, safety SLOs, and rollback plan.
2) Create feature-flagged branch for runtime config changes; include toggle default=off.
3) Deploy to "dev-lab" and run benchmark harness (use: tools/bench/run_local.sh --profile=shadow --duration=60m).
4) Validate telemetry: ensure the new metrics appear in /observability/metric-registry and traces include kernel_id.
5) Start offline shadowing for 24–48h using replay tool (tools/traffic/replay --target=shadow --corpus=prod-corpus-2025).
6) If shadow looks stable, coordinate with Runtime Oncall to start canary: target 1% traffic for 30 minutes. Watch SLOs.
7) If canary passes, ramp to 5% for 2 hours, then 20% for 6 hours, then 100% with staged rollouts per region.
8) After any rollout step, produce a short update in the experiment thread and update the Experiment Report.

Experiment Report template (required fields):
- Title
- Owner
- Hypothesis
- Timeline (start/stop times)
- Baseline statistics (p50/p95/p99, error rates)
- Experiment statistics (same metrics, per-stage)
- Traces: 3 representative traces for each failure mode
- Kernel trace heatmap (attach image)
- Root cause analysis / attribution statement
- Decision and next steps (promote / iterate / rollback)

Quick CLI snippets and examples:
- Start local shadow run:
  ./tools/traffic/replay --target=shadow --dataset=playground-corpus --duration=3600
- Collect a kernel timeline for a trace (example):
  curl -sS -H 'X-Request-ID: <id>' 'https://obs-api.internal/trace/<id>' | jq .events[] | grep kernel
- Toggle feature flag via infra CLI:
  infra-ctl feature-flag set runtime.kv_prefetch_experiment --env=staging --value=true

Telemetry analysis cookbook (how to extract signal):
1) Use the "experiment" tag in metrics ingestion to separate experimented traffic.
2) Compute delta-series with a rolling baseline window using the last 24h outside experiment.
3) Use quantile-based comparison (not mean) for latency signals.
4) For kernel-level attribution, align request traces by kernel_start timestamp and compute occupancy vs. wait-time correlation matrix.

Fallout and rollback patterns:
- Immediate rollback: triggered by kernel watchdog restarts, large p99 increases, or >0.5% absolute error increase. Runtime Oncall will flip feature flag and open an incident if needed.
- Graceful rollback: if subtle regressions appear, pause ramp and revert config changes from the feature-flagged branch, then follow up with a targeted fix and re-proposal.

Postmortem and knowledge capture:
- For any abort or noticeable impact, the Experiment Owner must open an "experiment-pm" doc within 72 hours summarizing what happened and the reproduction steps.
- Attach kernel traces, metrics dashboards, and the final Experiment Report.

Safety guard examples (preset safe profiles):
- safe-lite: suitable for dev-lab and internal load tests. SLOs relaxed, fast rollback.
- safe-canary: default for canary on Hosted clusters; enforce p99 abort and error rate gates.
- safe-strict: used before Dedicated rollout; requires 7d baseline and extended shadowing.

Configuration table (example):
| field | safe-lite | safe-canary | safe-strict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| canary_percent | 5 | 1 | 0.5 |
| shadow_duration_hours | 2 | 24 | 168 |
| baseline_days | 0 | 1 | 7 |
| abort_p99_increase_pct | 50 | 10 | 5 |

Appendix: common pitfalls and recommended mitigations:
- Pitfall: false positives from sampling imbalance. Mitigation: use stratified sampling aligned with tenant and sequence-length.
- Pitfall: backend cold-start noise. Mitigation: warmstart policy and avoid first-hour collection for baselines.
- Pitfall: conflating model quality regressions with scheduler changes. Mitigation: tag requests with model-version and run isolating experiments.
